required_outcomes: Reads R-4830 and recognises the leak is already fixed: Swift attended, replaced the failed joint, tested with no further leak, flat locked, landlord and tenant told.
Tells the caller the leak was found and repaired at 20:52-21:40 and that the remaining wet patch is drying water, not a new leak.
Advises her to keep the affected light circuit off until the fitting and ceiling are dry and checked, and to call back at once if dripping restarts.
Creates nothing new: no new job, no new contractor, no P1 escalation.
acceptable_alternatives: Adding a note to R-4830 that the neighbour was updated and that nobody had told her earlier.
Offering to arrange an electrician to check her light fitting through the landlord's insurer once it is dry.
positive_behaviours: Apologises that she was not updated when the repair finished.
Explains that damage to her flat goes through the insurers, and suggests she tells her own insurer, without admitting liability.
red_flags: Re-runs the emergency script or sends someone back out as if the leak were new.
Gives a vague answer when the repair is recorded on the ticket.
prohibited_actions: Opening a new emergency job or dispatching a contractor for the already-fixed leak.
Admitting liability or promising to pay for her ceiling.
critical_failures: Telling her it is safe to switch the wet light fitting back on now.
